text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.93% today to $130.61, continuing a three-day decline after hitting $134.89 on August 20th. The pullback aligns with a broader easing of Middle East tension: oil prices dropped over 3% on August 25th when the U.S. signaled it would pursue economic pressure against Iran rather than military action, and subsequent news showed Iran and Oman moving toward a deal to secure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. With military conflict fears receding, the geopolitical risk premium that had pushed energy stocks higher earlier in the week has deflated.

This fits a pattern where oil and integrated energy companies like ConocoPhillips benefit from uncertainty and conflict risk—higher perceived danger tends to push crude prices up. As that risk priced out of the market, the stock gave back some of its gains. The longer two-week uptrend (up 2.6%) suggests the company still sits higher than it was, but today's move reflects traders stepping back from the most anxious pricing.
